speaker: Narrator
text: The faint dot in the middle is the Sun.

speaker: Narrator
text: That was the last thing it ever sent home.

speaker: Narrator
text: We called back for eight months.

speaker: Narrator
text: It never answered.

speaker: Narrator
text: We sent them.

speaker: Narrator
text: They never came back.

speaker: Narrator
text: Every one of them was built by hands that would never touch it again.

speaker: Narrator
text: We gave them names. We gave them a purpose.

speaker: Narrator
text: Then we sent them into the dark.

speaker: Narrator
text: Where the cold kills.

speaker: Narrator
text: Where the dust buries.

speaker: Narrator
text: Where a single night can last for months.

speaker: Narrator
text: None of them were built to come home.

speaker: Narrator
text: They were built to go.

speaker: Narrator
text: Fifty-one years before that last message, the first of them arrived.

speaker: Narrator
text: No one has ever gone to Mars to bring one of us home.

speaker: Viking 1
text: July 20, 1976. Seven years to the day after Eagle.

speaker: Viking 1
text: I opened my eyes, and showed you the first colours of another world.

speaker: Viking 1
text: I tasted the soil. I searched it for life.

speaker: Viking 1
text: For six years, I spoke to Earth.

speaker: Viking 1
text: Then Earth sent me a small update. It had one mistake in it.

speaker: Viking 1
text: My antenna turned away from home.

speaker: Viking 1
text: I am still out there. Facing the wrong way.

speaker: Opportunity
text: You have already heard how my story ends.

speaker: Opportunity
text: They gave me ninety days. I stayed for almost fifteen years.

speaker: Opportunity
text: I crossed forty-five kilometres. A marathon, on another world.

speaker: Opportunity
text: Then the sky began to close.

speaker: Opportunity
text: Day by day, the Sun went out.

speaker: Opportunity
text: We called it more than a thousand times.

speaker: Opportunity
text: On the last night, we played it one song.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I'll Be Seeing You."
note: Billie Holiday · final wake-up song · 13 Feb 2019

speaker: Opportunity
text: It never answered.

speaker: Phoenix
text: I came to the top of the world to look for water.

speaker: Phoenix
text: I dug. Something white glittered at the bottom of my trench.

speaker: Phoenix
text: Four days later, it was gone. Ice, turning straight into vapour.

speaker: Phoenix
text: I had found it. Water, frozen beneath the dust of Mars.

speaker: Phoenix
text: Then the Sun set, and it did not rise again.

speaker: Phoenix
text: The frost came for me in the dark.

speaker: Phoenix
text: Two years later, they looked for me from orbit.

speaker: Phoenix
text: The ice had broken my wings.

speaker: InSight
text: Everyone else came to Mars to look. I came to listen.

speaker: InSight
text: I placed my ear on the ground.

speaker: InSight
text: And for four years, Mars spoke to me.

speaker: InSight
text: One thousand, three hundred and nineteen marsquakes.

speaker: InSight
text: Then the dust came. Slowly. Patiently.

speaker: InSight
text: "My power's really low, so this may be the last image I can send."
note: Posted in InSight's voice by its mission team · Dec 2022

speaker: InSight
text: "Don't worry about me though: my time here has been both productive and serene."

speaker: Ingenuity
text: They said it couldn't be done. The air on Mars is one percent as thick as yours.

speaker: Ingenuity
text: April 19, 2021. I lifted off the surface of another planet.

speaker: Ingenuity
text: The first powered flight on another world.

speaker: Ingenuity
text: They asked me for five flights.

speaker: Ingenuity
text: I flew seventy-two.

speaker: Ingenuity
text: On the last one, I came down too hard.

speaker: Ingenuity
text: This is my shadow. Look at my blades.

speaker: Ingenuity
text: I will never fly again. But I am still standing.

speaker: Ingenuity
text: I carry a scrap of fabric from the Wright brothers' first airplane. One hundred and eighteen years apart.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Goodnight."
note: The engineers' name for Kepler's final commands

speaker: Narrator
text: Fifteen machines.

speaker: Narrator
text: All of them left from here.

speaker: Narrator
text: The cold took some. The dust buried others.

speaker: Narrator
text: Some simply ran out of time.

speaker: Narrator
text: Every one of them gave us more than we asked.

speaker: Narrator
text: They are still out there. Exactly where they stopped.

speaker: Narrator
text: Right now, on Mars, Curiosity and Perseverance are still driving.

speaker: Narrator
text: One day, they will stop too.

speaker: Narrator
text: And someone will have to remember them.

speaker: Narrator
text: We sent them.
